# Name-day research sources

This is the shared, growing directory for LV, LT and EE name-history research. Read it before a new round. Use [NAMEDAYS_BACKLOG.md](NAMEDAYS_BACKLOG.md) for the calendar queue, [NAMEDAYS.md](NAMEDAYS.md) for editorial/data rules, and the [round notes](research/namedays/) for individual claims and outcomes. Source URLs belong here and in working files/provenance, never in the widget interface.

Last directory review: **14 November 2026**, including the completed first annual calendar-order research pass through **11 November** (all 366 calendar dates, including 29 February) and the rounds 56–61 verification recheck of every open 12 November–25 December profile. Resource IDs below are stable references for research notes. A useful catalogue or repository is a place to search, not evidence for every name it contains.

## Start here

0. Check the consolidated [source index](NAMEDAYS_SOURCE_INDEX.md) first: one row per source ID with the rounds and names that cite it, and its full URL/name list in `research/namedays/source-index.csv`. Search every cached PDF at once with `node scripts/nameday-source-cache.mjs search --query NAME --word true`. Regenerate the index with `npm run sources:namedays` after adding sources or round notes.
1. Search the exact NFC spelling, keeping diacritics. Try a second query without them only to discover candidates. Search the source language too: `personvārds`, `vārda izcelsme`, `vardas`, `kilmė`, `eesnimi`, `päritolu`.
2. Look for an exact dictionary entry or an explicit spelling correspondence. Read academic onomastics when the older dictionary lacks a form. Its absence does not prove that the name was unused.
3. Find a separate dated historical, archival, literary or professional episode. Identify whether it concerns this spelling, a documented related form, or a fictional character.
4. Search the existing private page index first; see [NAMEDAYS_PDF_CACHE.md](NAMEDAYS_PDF_CACHE.md). Index a new reusable PDF once. Inspect the original PDF page for diacritics, table columns, captions and author/date. Search-engine snippets and PDF text layers can drop or misread letters. Record both PDF and printed page numbers.
5. Save the exact URL, title/author/year, checked page or section, supported claim, limitations, outcome and next step in the next numbered round notes. Keep raw PDFs, HTML, OCR and screenshots in private `var/namedays-research/`.
6. A working comparison stays `needs_more` / `unverified`, even when a source independently establishes the spelling's use. Separate established facts from the unresolved inference. Do not transfer first attestations, calendar-entry years, biographies or population counts between forms.
7. Check the core references for the country before the web (all cached and searchable; details in their rows below). **LV:** LV-SILINS90 (the printed Siliņš 1990 itself; printed page = PDF page − 3), LV-SILINS (catalogue pages), LV-LPVV (historical dictionary, browser pane only, 219 entries), LV-BALODIS08 (2008 thesis; garbled ģ/ļ/ņ/ķ), LV-BALODE22-TENDENCES, LV-PLESUMA-BALODE13, LVA rendering records. **LT:** LT-SALYS83 (1964 calendar pairs and Jurgis-type histories), LT-BUGA-RR1 (Būga’s 1911 personal-name study; hyphenated stems) and LT-BUGA-RR4 (index), LT-ZINKEVICIUS77 (17th-century Vilnius registers; search Polish spellings too), LT-PAKERYS09/10/11, LT-LPZ (surname dictionary), LT-FRAENKEL62 (lexical roots only), LT-VU-ELABA-34081137, LT-ZINKEVICIUS09-SAVEIKA, LT-VU-ELABA-115477061. **EE:** EE-RAJANDI66, EE-MAGISTE36 (1936 list with kstl./tarv. labels), EE-MAGISTE29-AES, EE-KURRIK1901 (page images only), EE-OMAKEEL-2011-2-03 (Lihula Wackenbuch counts). Still missing and worth acquiring: Kuzavinis & Savukynas, *Lietuvių vardų kilmės žodynas* (6th ed. 2009, ISBN 9785420016480); Tõnisson calendars 1884/1886; Teppo-Vilkuna 1947.
8. Books the user downloads are registered with `index` into the private cache and never copied into this repository. Sites that render entries only in the browser are read in the browser pane as a visitor; LV-LPVV is already fully cached from the user’s authorized snapshot (LV-LPVV-<id>), so search the cache instead. If `pdftoppm` is unavailable, render page images with PyMuPDF.

[Article](https://journals.lki.lt/actalinguisticalithuanica/article/view/2518), [PDF p. 6](https://journals.lki.lt/actalinguisticalithuanica/article/download/2518/2474/#page=6), DOI `10.35321/all93-01`. | Direct discussion of Jevgenija / Jevgeņija and Jevgenijs / Jevgēnijs / Jevgeņijs. | LV-IDENTITY25 | Balode and Siliņa-Piņķe, **Reflection of Identity in Given Names of Latvia Over the Last Century**, *Onomastica Uralica* 17 (2025), pp. 139–156. Exact spelling visually checked. | Juozapotas is on 12 November in the supplied project calendar. Preserve the discrepancy, not an automatic calendar correction. This record establishes usage/short forms, not a proved etymological bridge to Juozapatas or a coining date. |

## Productive sources for 15 November

| ID | Resource and checked location | Supported claim and limits |

| EE-MAGISTE29 | Julius Mägiste, *Eestipäraseid isikunimesid*, Tartu, 1929. [Publisher record](https://www.emakeeleselts.ee/valjaanne/eestiparaseid-isikunimesid/); [ETERA PDF p. 22 / printed p. 20](https://www.etera.ee/api/oai2/download/10343.pdf#page=22). | Visually checked exact **Vaige**, German gloss **ruhig, still**, and explicit comparison with **Vaike** in the feminine list. Publication is dated by the publisher record. Does not establish Vaigi/Vaiki, a unique derivation direction, a coining date or first birth. |
| LT-LMTA | Lithuanian Academy of Music and Theatre, [History of the Department of Organ and Harpsichord](https://old.lmta.lt/en/fakultetas/muzikos-fakultetas/vargonu-ir-klavesino-katedra/veikla-ir-istorija/), opening historical paragraphs. | Exact **Leopoldas Digrys**: the organ class closed in 1949 and reopened in 1962 on his initiative. Direct HTML fetch succeeded despite the web reader's cache miss. This is an institutional history, not name etymology or a first-name attestation. |
| LV-AUDIT | State Audit Office, [Riga property-management discussion](https://www.lrvk.gov.lv/lv/jaunumi/rigas-domes-nekustamo-ipasumu-parvaldiba-ka-ir-bijis-lidz-sim-un-ka-vajadzetu-but-turpmak), participant paragraph. | Exact **Undalgs Mētra** professional-use example. Supports the given name's use, not an etymology; no publication year is inferred from a search engine's relative timestamp. Undalgs remains unverified. |

Round 15 also visually checked **LT-SALYS83**, [PDF p. 284 / printed p. 269](https://tautosmenta.lt/wp-content/uploads/lituanistika/Salys_1983_LT.pdf#page=284): the essay *Mūsų lietuviškieji vardai* prefers older **Vaidilas** over calendar **Vaidilis**. The 1983 collected volume is the checked publication; the original essay's date is not inferred. [PDF p. 280 / printed p. 265](https://tautosmenta.lt/wp-content/uploads/lituanistika/Salys_1983_LT.pdf#page=280) records **Žadvydas** as a masculine given name and surname in a German–Lithuanian dictionary appendix. This is a related-form episode for Žadvydė, not her first attestation. The 15 November calendar on p. 317 instead has Vaidila (Vaidys) and Žada; these are not silently substituted for the project's names.

**LT-VLE** directly pairs [Leopoldas II with Leopold II](https://www.vle.lt/straipsnis/leopoldas-ii/), providing the spelling bridge to the curated **INT-BTN** etymology. The exact **LT-GUIDE** Leopoldas page says its meaning is still being clarified; its mixed related-name list was not used as the bridge. **LT-INSTITUTIONS**: [Albertas Skyrelis](https://rasytojai.lt/rasytojai/skyrelis-albertas/), bibliography, dates *Velnio tuzinas* to 1977 and *Pabūk džiaugsmu* to 1987; direct fetch succeeded.

**LV-SILINS**: [Leopolds](https://www.izpetnieks.lv/en/name/Leopolds), p. 213, gives liut/bald, Mazsalaca in the last quarter of the nineteenth century and calendar 1767. [Unda](https://www.izpetnieks.lv/en/name/Unda), p. 312, gives Latin unda and Riga 1969 without a calendar-entry year. [Undīna](https://www.izpetnieks.lv/en/name/Und%C4%ABna) and [Undīne](https://www.izpetnieks.lv/en/name/Und%C4%ABne) reproduce the combined **Undīna/-e** entry, p. 312: Riga 1922 and calendar 1908 retain combined-entry scope. Neither date is transferred to unaccented Undina. **INT-SNL** [Undis, feminine name](https://snl.no/Undis_-_kvinnenamn), signed by Gulbrand Alhaug, explains a Norwegian feminine coinage in 1897 from Unn and dis; it does not establish Latvian masculine Undis. The [Fouqué article](https://snl.no/Friedrich_Heinrich_Karl_la_Motte_Fouqu%C3%A9) documents *Undine* (1811), but no claim of direct transmission to a Latvian family was accepted.

Unresolved leads: Leopoldina's Behind the Name result is user-submitted, while Duden's Leopoldina entry names an academy. Neither resolves the Latvian feminine name. Undija, Undita and Undalgs still need exact onomastic explanations. The **LV-LVA-LT** manual's printed p. 47 was inspected but contains no Leopoldas pair. The Vaigi/Vaiki blog and user-submitted lists are leads to Raivo Seppo's *Elavad nimed* (1994), whose relevant original entry still needs inspection through EE-ETERA/EE-DIGAR. Common-word **vaiki** is not itself a given-name etymology. All eight unresolved forms and concrete next steps are in `research/namedays/round15-notes.json` and the backlog.

Publication evidence refers to the 1983 collection, not an assumed coining date. Popular name-guide URLs for Vaišvydas and Gerdvilė did not yield usable exact entries in the direct fetch.

**EE-MAGISTE29**, [PDF p. 23 / printed p. 21](https://www.etera.ee/api/oai2/download/10343.pdf#page=23), visually confirms **Aarno (Finnish), compared with Häädemeeste Aarne**. INT-WIKTIONARY’s exact Estonian Aarne section says borrowed from Finnish; INT-BTN [Aarne](https://www.behindthename.com/name/aarne) links [Scandinavian Arne](https://www.behindthename.com/name/arne-1), Old Norse ǫrn. [German Arne](https://www.behindthename.com/name/arne-2) instead shortens Arnold. Preserve both documented Arne explanations rather than forcing a single route on every Estonian family. The EMIC Arne Oit pages returned 403, so work dates from their snippets were not used.

**LV-SILINS** checked entries: Banga p. 77 (Latvian banga; calendar 1925; personal record 1927), Glorija p. 139 (calendar 1915; personal record 1925; blank English origin field), Jefims pp. 177/109 (Eifēmija cross-reference; eighteenth-century Latgale; calendar 1899), Vētra p. 323 (Latvian vētra comparison; feminine Talsi-area use in the second quarter of the twentieth century; masculine 1936). **Landa and Landijs p. 207 remain explicitly questioned**: Madona 1973 and the combined Landis, -ijs first-quarter-of-the-twentieth-century record prove use only. Ganda supplies no defensible origin proposal and retains the ordinary missing-history display. All four open names and next steps are in `research/namedays/round16-notes.json` and the backlog.

## Productive sources for 17 November

| ID | Resource and checked location | Supported claim and limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| EE-EWOD | University of Tartu, *Estonian Writers’ Online Dictionary*: [Einar Maasik](https://ewod.ut.ee/m/maasik/), biography and bibliography; [Egon Rannet](https://ewod.ut.ee/et/r/egon-rannet/), biography and plays. | Einar Maasik: debut in **Edasi**, 1953; **Koduküla teel**, 1959; **Teekaaslane**, 1960. Egon Rannet: known as Eugen/Jevgeni Brücke until 1940; **Kadunud poeg**, 1958. An individual renaming does not establish a universal Egon/Eugen etymology. A guessed Einar Rannut URL returned 404 and was not evidence. |
| EE-SUVETEATER | Emajõe Suveteater, [Heinari tähetund](https://suveteater.ee/lavastused/heinari-tahetund), production synopsis. | Fictional theatre property worker **Heinar** explicitly distinguishes his name from Einar. The production is based on Eberhard Streul’s monodrama. Supports exact literary use, not etymology, a first attestation or a universal Heinar/Einar correspondence. Heinar remains unverified. |
| EE-CALENDAR-CHECK | [Statistics Estonia name-day list](https://stat.ee/nimed/NIMEPAEVAD), 10 May / 17 November; [Neanky Ainari](https://nimed.neanky.ee/et/nimi/Ainari), exact page. | The official list places **Aino** in the 10 May group and **Eino/Einari** in the 17 November group. The project’s supplied calendar and the secondary list instead include **Aino/Ainari** on 17 November. Record the discrepancy and preserve supplied membership/date in this research round. Neanky’s zero-or-under-five Ainari result is not proof of zero bearers or etymology. No variant relationship is inferred from co-membership. |

**LT-SALYS83** pages visually checked in round 17: [PDF p. 224 / printed p. 209](https://tautosmenta.lt/wp-content/uploads/lituanistika/Salys_1983_LT.pdf#page=224) separates deity **Dionisas** from personal names **Dionyzas und Dionizas → Dionys(ius)**. [PDF p. 317 / printed p. 302](https://tautosmenta.lt/wp-content/uploads/lituanistika/Salys_1983_LT.pdf#page=317) records **Getautas (Getas), Gilvilė (Gilva)** on 17 November in the 1964 calendar reprinted in 1983. [PDF p. 288 / printed p. 273](https://tautosmenta.lt/wp-content/uploads/lituanistika/Salys_1983_LT.pdf#page=288) places related masculine **Gilvilas** under **(su)gilti, gildyti (širdį)**, contrasting with LT-GUIDE’s **gilus** explanation for Gilvilė. Its precise derivation remains open; the male stem analysis is not silently transferred to the female entry. The [1994 LKI article 1463/1557](https://journals.lki.lt/actalinguisticalithuanica/article/download/1463/1557/) is an uninspected further lead, not accepted evidence.

**LT-VLE** [Salomėja Nėris](https://www.vle.lt/straipsnis/salomeja-neris/) confirms *Anksti rytą* (1927) and the first pen-name signature **Neris**, later **Nėris**, on *Pajūry*, *Ateitis* no. 11 (1923). Keep the surname pen name distinct from the given name. **LT-GUIDE** directly supplies Getautas’s ge-/taut- and Salomėja’s Šlomit/shalom explanations. Its Dionyzas “divine tree” proposal is not accepted as a verified whole-name translation; INT-BTN [Dionysios](https://www.behindthename.com/name/dionysios) supplies the documented connection to Dionysos. No ultimate breakdown of the deity’s name is claimed. The guessed VLE Dionyzas Poška URL returned 404 and supplied no biography.

**EE-MAGISTE29**, [PDF p. 13 / printed p. 11](https://www.etera.ee/api/oai2/download/10343.pdf#page=13), visually confirms feminine **Aino**, related forms and German **die einzige**. INT-WIKTIONARY’s exact Estonian section says borrowed from Finnish; publication in 1929 is not a coining date. **INT-SNL**: Gulbrand Alhaug’s [Egil name article](https://snl.no/Egil_-_mannsnamn) discusses Egill, respect/awe and sword edge; [Egils saga](https://snl.no/Egils_saga) tentatively dates composition before 1240 and the main Möðruvallabók manuscript to the first half of the fourteenth century. Preserve uncertainty, the Icelandic literary context and the distinction from an Estonian first attestation. The [ETERA 22289 Heinar naming-study lead](https://www.etera.ee/api/oai2/download/22289.pdf) returned 404; its snippet and user-submitted variant lists were not used as proof.

**LV-SILINS**: Hugo p. 156 gives hugu and exact calendar 1767 / personal record 1871. Uga, Uģis and Ugo p. 311 directly refer to Hugo but keep their own records: **Uga, Riga 1895, calendar 1925; Uģis, Riga 1937, calendar 1925; Ugo, Riga 1940, no calendar-entry year**. INT-BTN’s curated Hugh/Hugo entries corroborate the family and explicitly list Uģis. Victor Hugo is a surname example, not a first-name attestation. **Higo** remains a tentative Hugo comparison with no usable dated record. **Igo**, pp. 158/156, is placed under Hugo but also carries a questioned Ignāts connection; its first-quarter-of-twentieth-century record establishes use only. Do not infer a general Igor etymology from a singer’s stage name or treat Ignāts/ignis as settled. All five unresolved names and next steps are in `research/namedays/round17-notes.json` and the backlog.

Useful for tracing the lexical family and its bibliography. **Common-word evidence only**: it does not establish the personal names Brīve/Brīvīte, their derivation, or a coining date. |

**LV-SILINS**, exact catalogue entries: [Doloresa](https://www.izpetnieks.lv/en/name/Doloresa), p. 100, gives Latin dolor, personal record **1930**, calendar **1964**. [Brīva](https://www.izpetnieks.lv/en/name/Br%C4%ABva), p. 87, gives brīvs/brīvība, personal **1931**, calendar **1908**. [Dolita](https://www.izpetnieks.lv/en/name/Dolita) and [Dollija](https://www.izpetnieks.lv/en/name/Dollija), pp. 100–101, belong to Dolly/Doroteja, Greek dōron/theos: **Dolita, Alūksne, third quarter of the twentieth century; Dollija, 1923**. Neither has a calendar-entry year. [Laisve](https://www.izpetnieks.lv/en/name/Laisve), p. 206, gives Lithuanian laisvė, personal **second quarter of the twentieth century**, calendar **1931**; retain exact Latvian e. [Latvis](https://www.izpetnieks.lv/en/name/Latvis), p. 209, gives the Latvian nationality word, personal **1942**, calendar **1902**. [Latvīte](https://www.izpetnieks.lv/en/name/Latv%C4%ABte), p. 209, directly refers to Latvis but has its own **second-quarter-of-twentieth-century** record and no calendar-entry year. [Zanders](https://www.izpetnieks.lv/en/name/Zanders), pp. 334/283, explicitly refers through **Sanderss** to Aleksandrs: personal **last quarter of the nineteenth century**, calendar **1783**. The prose has Sanderss while the related list has Sanders; do not silently regularize the reference. **INT-BTN** curated [Dolores](https://www.behindthename.com/name/dolores), [Dolly](https://www.behindthename.com/name/dolly) and [Alexander](https://www.behindthename.com/name/alexander) support family context, without transferring dates or establishing a unique route into Latvia.

**LT-GUIDE** exact [Ginvydas](https://www.tevu-darzelis.lt/vaiku-vardai/ginvydas/) and [Ginvydė](https://www.tevu-darzelis.lt/vaiku-vardai/ginvyde/) explain **gin- / ginti, gina** and **vyd- / (iš)vydo**. Their historical paragraph uses LT-ELTA-CALENDAR’s dated press record. No exact Ginvydas/Ginvydė entry was found in the inspected Salys text. Commercial generated-looking claims about famous bearers were not accepted without primary confirmation. [Otas](https://www.tevu-darzelis.lt/vaiku-vardai/otas/) and [Otonas](https://www.tevu-darzelis.lt/vaiku-vardai/otonas/) supply the Germanic family connection, corroborated by curated **INT-BTN** [Otto](https://www.behindthename.com/name/otto); unsupported popular Greek-ear explanations were rejected.

**LT-SALYS83** pages visually checked: [PDF p. 310 / printed p. 295](https://tautosmenta.lt/wp-content/uploads/lituanistika/Salys_1983_LT.pdf#page=310) has the heading **LIEPA**, day **2**, and **Otonas (Otas)** in the 1964 calendar reprinted in 1983. This is **2 July**, not 30 June from nearby extracted context, and differs from the project’s 18 November. Preserve project membership/date; use this page for the explicit form relationship. [PDF p. 263 / printed p. 248](https://tautosmenta.lt/wp-content/uploads/lituanistika/Salys_1983_LT.pdf#page=263) gives **Romanas → Roman(us)** and **Romas** as a short form of both **Romanas and Romualdas**. Do not rename Romas-only bearers Romanas. **LT-VLE** [Otonas I](https://www.vle.lt/straipsnis/otonas-i/) explicitly pairs him with **Otto I**, Holy Roman emperor **962–973**: a foreign historical example in Lithuanian, not a Lithuanian ruler or domestic first attestation.

**EE-MAGISTE29**, [PDF p. 15 / printed p. 13](https://www.etera.ee/api/oai2/download/10343.pdf#page=15), visually confirms **Ilo** in the feminine list, German **freude, freudebringerin**, joy / bringer of joy. The following line is **Ilts-u**, not Ilu. **INT-WIKTIONARY**’s exact [Estonian Ilo section](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/Ilo#Estonian) instead derives it from **ilu**, beauty/splendour. Keep the distinct explanatory records rather than inventing a merged meaning or assuming the Finnish route. **POP-EE**’s opened [exact ILO statistics](https://www.stat.ee/nimed/ILO) records **23 men and 15 women on 1 January 2026**, and 18 November membership; the narrative uses only the both-sex fact. The dictionary’s masculine label does not negate historical and official female use.

The separate **LV-SILINS** [Latvian Ilo entry](https://www.izpetnieks.lv/en/name/Ilo), p. 161, supplies the inherited raw attestation “13th century, Ikšķile / third quarter of the 20th century, Cēsis” and cautions against combining records without a gender distinction. It discusses tentative Elias/Ilū comparisons. Neither its dates nor these tentative Latvian routes establish the Estonian name’s origin or first use. The formatter now keeps the first record’s century independent of the later record’s quarter; the raw source text and Latvian scope remain intact.

Unresolved exact forms: **Brīve/Brīvīte** catalogue p. 87 leaves origin unresolved and refers to Brīva; **Aleksandris/Alesandrs** pages point to an Aleksandrs explanation on p. 49 rather than establishing the exact forms; **Zandars** points to Zanders/Sanderss material on pp. 334/283. Exact **LV-LVA** searches using `search?locale=lv&words=on&sources=on&q=NAME` returned no entries for all five; absence is not proof of nonexistence. **Ilu** has no checked exact etymology: its Wiktionary URL returned 404, EKI direct fetch returned 403, and neither common-word ilu nor the Ilo entry proves a variant route. All six retain labelled hypotheses and individual next steps in `research/namedays/round18-notes.json` and backlog. Previously open names remain pending.

| ID | Resource | What it can establish |
| --- | --- | --- |
| INT-BTN | [Behind the Name](https://www.behindthename.com/). | Curated etymologies and explicit variants; follow the full chain to its linguistic root. User submissions, forum guesses, popularity ratings and personality impressions are not equivalent evidence. |
| INT-WIKTIONARY | [Wiktionary](https://en.wiktionary.org/), e.g. [Kristo, Estonian section](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/Kristo#Estonian). | Exact national-language entries, short forms and references. Select the right language section; homonyms in Finnish, Albanian or Japanese do not prove an Estonian origin. Check dictionary citations where supplied. |
| INT-SNL | [Store norske leksikon](https://snl.no/), e.g. [Krister](https://snl.no/Krister_-_mannsnamn). | Signed name-scholar articles and concrete cultural examples. Norwegian literary history must remain identified as Norwegian. |

Preserve snapshot date and the component-count definition. |
| POP-EE | [Statistics Estonia names](https://stat.ee/nimed/), e.g. [Krister](https://stat.ee/nimed/KRISTER). | Exact first-name counts and published suppression limits. Do not substitute Latvia's component-count definition. |
| POP-LT | [Registrų centras](https://www.registrucentras.lt/) TOP 50 snapshots used by the existing LT updater. | Published popularity lists within their stated population/time scope. Absence from a TOP 50 list is not proof of zero bearers. |

## Sources that did not resolve the current gaps

The 12 November rare LV names produced calendar-list matches, surname matches and unrelated common words. In particular, Vidavs as a surname does not establish the given name's origin. The VVC list confirms membership but leaves the five origins open.

For the remaining 13 November spellings, neither a shared day nor a nearby name in a catalogue proves a spelling correspondence. Automatic aggregators may merge Jevgenijs and Jevgeņijs, then display the latter's count under the former. Use such pages only to locate their underlying reference. Do not import merged counts, generic personality text, AI etymologies, greeting-shop descriptions or a search-result snippet as verified history.

Juozapotas now has an exact historical calendar record, but the proposed Juozapatas etymological bridge remains unverified. Commercial pages offer inconsistent derivations; do not collapse Joseph and Josaphat families on that basis. Its next step is an authoritative dictionary or explicit historical paired-form record, not another calendar listing.

Round 164 (17 November 2026): Estonian Wikipedia name articles such as *Halliki* (cached as WEB-ET-WIKIPEDIA-ORG-WIKI-HALLIKI) give only bearer counts, rank and namesakes, with no origin; they are not productive for histories. For new Estonian names, the body text of EE-RAJANDI66 (pages before the index, about PDF 1–189) is productive: it gives name groups (nature names, sister and brother names), variants and base names. Search it with `var/namedays-research/rajandi164.cjs`.

Productive working mirror for the previously failed old journal download `1312/1230`. Supports scholarly disagreement, not a settled whole-name translation. Follow its dictionary references. |

Does **not** establish **giria**, an inventor, or a coining date. Web reader received a challenge, but direct PDF download succeeded and the page was rendered. |

**LV-SILINS**, exact pages: [Ando](https://www.izpetnieks.lv/en/name/Ando) and [Andijs](https://www.izpetnieks.lv/en/name/Andijs), p. 56, explicitly connect to Andrejs, directly or through Andis. The catalogue gives **Ando: Ventspils 1969**, separately **1975 frequency data**; **Andijs: Saldus district 1973**. Keep these records distinct. Page 335 gives **Zeltīte → zelts**, calendar **1908**, and **Zelta: Blome 1931**. Page 339 gives **Zlata → Bulgarian/Serbo-Croatian zlato**, with a catalogue 1973 record. Page 326 gives **Vilfrīds: willo/fridu**, first-quarter twentieth-century usage and calendar **1966**; **Vilibalds: willo/bald**, first-quarter twentieth-century usage and calendar **1767**. **Viliberts** refers to **Vilberts**, willo/beraht: retain the **shared-entry** scope of **1894/1966**, not an independent first record for each spelling.

Pages 324–325 do not settle **Vigors/Vigorts**. **Vigurds** has a **1928** usage record but its **Wigwart (?) / wīgan / wart** explanation remains questioned. Page 326 does not establish exact feminine short-i **Vilfrida**, and p. 335 does not establish **Zeltiņa**. Exact catalogue **Andars, Andejs, Vigra** pages offer no origin/citation. **LV-LVA** exact searches returned no corresponding rows for these unresolved forms; Andars/Andejs substring matches belong to other names and were rejected. None of these absences proves that a name was unused.

**LT-SIRENA15**, [PDF p. 1](https://rokiskiosirena.lt/laikrastis/2015-11-20.pdf#page=1), visually checked **Rytoj** list in the **20 November 2015** issue: **Gomantas, Eibartė, Honorijus, Alberta, Norgaudas, Girenė, Honoratas, Tomas**. Tomorrow means **21 November**. This documents exact spellings and a dated calendar use; it does not prove their origins. **LT-SALYS83**, [PDF p. 319 / printed p. 304](https://tautosmenta.lt/wp-content/uploads/lituanistika/Salys_1983_LT.pdf#page=319), instead gives **21 December**: **Honoratas (Honas, Noras), Girenė (Girė), Norgaudas (Noras)** in the 1964 calendar reprinted in 1983. Preserve the discrepancy and supplied project dates. [PDF p. 287 / printed p. 272](https://tautosmenta.lt/wp-content/uploads/lituanistika/Salys_1983_LT.pdf#page=287) places **Nórgaudas** under **Gaud-: gauti**; it does not justify selecting popular gaudus/gaudyti explanations. November’s **Eibarė** lacks the t of **Eibartė** and was rejected as an exact spelling bridge.

**LT-GUIDE**, opened exact Alberta/Eibartė/Honoratas/Honorijus entries, plus curated **INT-BTN** Alberta/Albert and Honoratus/Honorius support the stated linguistic families. Alberta’s adal/berht are separate elements, not a literal pedigree claim; Eibartė’s ei-/eiti and bart-/bartis are not a forced sentence. **LT-VLE** [Honorijus](https://www.vle.lt/straipsnis/honorijus/) explicitly pairs **Flavijus Honorijus / Flavius Honorius**, with the **393 Augustus title**. Use that dated Roman example; do not reuse its problematic Ravenna chronology. The Norgaudas guide explicitly says its meaning is being clarified; Girenė’s exact guide page returned 404. Popular forest explanations and user-submitted entries are leads only. Lrytas calendar pages returned 403 and were not accepted from snippets.

**INT-WIKTIONARY** exact [Pilvi, Estonian](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/Pilvi#Estonian) and [Pilve, Estonian](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/Pilve#Estonian) derive both feminine names from **pilv, cloud**. Keep Finnish and Estonian sections separate. **EE-MAGISTE29**, visually checked [PDF p. 20 / printed p. 18](https://www.etera.ee/api/oai2/download/10343.pdf#page=20), prints exact feminine **Pilvi** in **1929**. This prevents transferring the Finnish mid-twentieth-century invention claim into Estonian. The abbreviation was not expanded without its legend. For **Pilve**, 1929 is explicitly a **related Pilvi** episode, not an exact Pilve attestation. Surname matches for Pilve were not used as given-name evidence.

| INT-BURNEY1782 | Frances Burney, [*Cecilia, or Memoirs of an Heiress*, vol. 1, primary text](https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/6346/pg6346-images.html), front matter and Book I chapter i; [NYPL manuscript catalogue record](https://old-digitalcollections.nypl.org/items/b26cada0-5f86-0131-ba4d-58d385a7b928). | Primary text identifies fictional **Cecilia Beverley** and the surname condition attached to her inheritance. Reprint front matter explicitly gives the original **1782** edition; NYPL independently dates its manuscript item **1782**, not a claimed held printed copy. Gutenberg’s **2004** release is not first publication. Exact Cecilia episode; explicitly **related full-form** episode for Silja, not either name’s first Estonian use or a proven influence on Estonian parents. Ignore Gutenberg’s automatically generated summary. |
| INT-NERGAARD | Norwegian singer **Silje Nergaard**, [official biography](https://www.siljenergaard.com/bio), opening paragraphs. | Debut single **Tell Me Where You’re Going**, **1990**, recorded with **Pat Metheny**. Exact given-name professional episode, explicitly Norwegian. No current sales record, album total or first Estonian use is inferred. |

**LV-SILINS**, p. **50**: combined **Alfon/s, -ss** gives **Bikava 1877**, calendar **1817**, and competing **adal/al + funs** explanations. Keep both exact forms unverified while their dated usage is recorded. **Alfonija** refers to Alfons but labels its **Skaņkalne, last quarter of the nineteenth century (Bgr.)** record possible. Do not transfer masculine calendar dates. Exact **Alfins** page says the original has **Alfīns**, long ī; the long-ī catalogue URL returned 404 and no exact rendering bridge was found. Page **48**, combined **Aldr/a, -e**, questions both **alderīgs** and phonetic formation; **Kurzeme 1943** is usage evidence only. Page **328**, exact **Vilonija**, supplies **Greek philon** and **Jasmuiža 1925**; retain the Greek-word gloss rather than inventing a full-name translation.

Exact **Aldris/Aldijs** catalogue pages contain no usable origin/citation. **LV-LVA** returns no exact word rows for them; the Aldijs search’s **Garibaldijs** result is a rejected substring match. Aldra/Alfonija/Alfins/Vilonija searches also produced no exact rendering rows. These access/coverage gaps are not evidence of nonexistence. The Vilora catalogue’s old Veliev dissertation host failed DNS, and the guessed modern replacement returned 404; neither was accepted as read evidence. Use the independently inspected Vrublevskaya source above instead.

**LT-SALYS83**, visually checked [PDF p. 317 / printed p. 302](https://tautosmenta.lt/wp-content/uploads/lituanistika/Salys_1983_LT.pdf#page=317), gives **Cecilija (Cilė)** and **Steikintas (Steikys)** on **22 November**, in the **1964** calendar reprinted **1983**. Do not substitute **Steigintas** for **Steikintas**. [PDF p. 295 / printed p. 280](https://tautosmenta.lt/wp-content/uploads/lituanistika/Salys_1983_LT.pdf#page=295) lists **Stei(g)-: steigti ‘stengtis’**, including **Steikintas**. [PDF p. 284 / printed p. 269](https://tautosmenta.lt/wp-content/uploads/lituanistika/Salys_1983_LT.pdf#page=284), the reprinted essay *Mūsų lietuviškieji vardai*, explicitly includes **Laimutis, -ė** among creative vocabulary-based calendar names. Reprint year is not an invention date. **LT-GUIDE** exact Laimutis gives **Laimas/Laimis → laimė**; Cecilija gives **Caecilius → caecus**. Cilė’s own guide page returned 404, resolved through Pavan/Salys. Dargintė/Steigintas guide proposals remain open for original dictionary verification; their guide dates **9 November / 28 August**, and Laimutis **12 August**, differ from the supplied **22 November**. Preserve supplied membership. The Lrytas 2021 calendar page returned 403 in direct fetch; snippets were not used as primary historical evidence.

**INT-BTN**, curated exact **Silja** explicitly covers Finnish and Estonian diminutive use of **Cecilia**; Cecilia continues **Caecilius/caecus**. **INT-SNL**, signed Gulbrand Alhaug articles for [Silja](https://snl.no/Silja_-_kvinnenamn), [Silje](https://snl.no/Silje_-_kvinnenamn) and [Sille](https://snl.no/Sille_-_kvinnenamn), explicitly connect the forms with Cecilia/Cecilie. Silje/Sille linguistic and cultural accounts are identified as **Nordic context**, not a universal borrowing path for Estonian families. Sille’s **nineteenth-century Vest-Agder** distribution explicitly includes variants such as **Cille**; do not present it as an exact-form count. Wiktionary’s Sille entry is Danish only and Silje Norwegian only; they are not exact Estonian language sections. The previously downloaded Saarelma-Paukkala/Hussar 2020 article, printed p. 107, discusses **Finnish** medieval Cecilia → Silja, not an Estonian borrowing date.

**Säsil** remains unverified: the [BTN proposal](https://www.behindthename.com/name/sa12sil/submitted) is user-submitted, not curated. The exact Wiktionary page could not be opened. **POP-EE**, [official name-day list](https://www.stat.ee/nimed/NIMEPAEVAD), confirms exact membership on **22 November**, not the proposed Cécile/Cecilia origin. Business, pet-name and similarly written surname results were rejected as given-name etymology.

## Keep this directory current

When a new source is productive, add or extend a row with a stable ID, direct link, provider, title/author/year, exact page/section, a named example, supported claim, access limitation and last review date. Put unresolved leads in the relevant limitations field, not among proven results. Link those IDs from the round notes and give unresolved names a concrete next search step.

Use the next numeric `round<N>-notes.json` so existing backlog precedence remains correct. Keep earlier rounds as history; the latest country-scoped note records the current outcome. After content changes, bump the writer, regenerate the affected country data and the backlog, then run the appropriate validation. Update [NAMEDAYS.md](NAMEDAYS.md), this directory and contributor instructions when the workflow changes. Continue using `codex/namedays-round4`.

**24 November.** LV-SILINS exact Velta p. 320, Velards/Veldra p. 319; Veldra’s cited gloss is Latvian veldre, a swampy depression, not an automatically substituted sense of lodged grain. **LT-SALYS83 PDF p. 308 / printed p. 293**, preceded by the May heading on PDF p. 307, gives **Gerardas (Geras) on 24 May**, unlike this project’s 24 November. **LT-PAKERYS11 PDF p. 2 / printed p. 91** explicitly has **Žýbartė** beside **Žýbartas**. **EE-LEOLE05 PDF p. 6** directly connects **Ustav/Ustus** with Estonian ustav/ustavus; [EKI ustav](https://sonaveeb.ee/search/unif/est%2Cother/dsall/ustav/1/est) corroborates the common-word sense. A file provisionally labelled `magiste1936` actually contained the 1929 edition and was not used as a 1936 source. The old LU Skulte thesis URL returned an HTML challenge locally, so no reusable PDF was obtained or local original-page check claimed; Kecija/Ķecija remains open.

**26 November.** Agency exact German **Konrad→Konrāds**, citing Ceplītis 1960 p. 62, is a given-name row, distinct from the Hungarian surname row. **Konrads** alone retains 1295/1767; **Sebastjans** retains 1545/1767, while **Sebastians** has a separate Norwegian rendering. **LT-SALYS83 PDF p. 265 / printed p. 250** explicitly lists feminine **Silva** as a short form of Silvija and masculine Silva as a short form of Silvestras; p. 317 has Dobilas on 26 November. **EE-MAGISTE29 PDF p. 18 / printed p. 16** has **Maare = Maria**, separately from **Maaret = Margareete**. **INT-SNL** [Dagmar](https://snl.no/Dagmar_-_kvinnenamn), by Gulbrand Alhaug, distinguishes Slavic Dragomira from its later Danish day/maiden reinterpretation. **27 November.** LV-SILINS p. 209 dates **Laurijs 1932**, referring to Laura. **Vinifreda** has competing routes: the older dictionary’s Germanic Vinfrīds comparison and the agency’s **English Winifred→Vinifreda**, whose Welsh history is different. **28 November.** LV-SILINS p. 254 gives **Olita 1906 / calendar 1915** and **Olina near Izvalta, 1943**; the shared **Ol(l)ija** entry does not give each spelling its own first date. **LT-SALYS83 PDF p. 92 / printed p. 77** discusses Jokūbas/Jakūbas and sixteenth-century inventory spellings; biblical heel imagery remains an explanatory narrative, not independent proof of a literal root. **PDF p. 318 / printed p. 303** gives **Rimgaudas (Rimas), Vakarė on 28 November**. **PDF p. 319 / printed p. 304** gives **Steponas (Stepas) on 26 December**, unlike the project’s November date. Curated INT-BTN Virginia and Ignatius entries distinguish unknown Roman roots from later maiden/fire associations. The catalogue’s **Virgilija** text does not resolve masculine **Virgilijs**. **LT-SALYS83 PDF p. 318** gives Daujotas (Daujys) on 29 November, but **Saturninas (Satas, Satys) on 15 December**. **PDF p. 265** identifies Saturninas as a personal name, whereas the Saturnas row is a planet name; do not confuse the categories.

**30 November.** Exact agency correspondences include **András→Andrāšs** (Sakse 1998 p. 50), **Андрій→Andrijs** (Hansons/Poļakova 2023 p. 148), and **Andrus→Andruss** (Raģe 1960 p. 52). Preserve Hungarian András versus Faroese Andras. LV-SILINS gives **Andreass 1462**, **Andress 1464**, and an exact Andrs entry. **EE-MAGISTE29 PDF p. 24 / printed p. 22**, visually checked, pairs **Ando/Andu** and identifies **Andre** as a Seto/South Estonian form by Andres/Andrei. **LT-PAKERYS11 PDF p. 8 / printed p. 97**, visually checked, has **Výtartė** beside Výtartas. **Dóvainė** on PDF p. 4 establishes the feminine spelling, not one of the competing second-stem meanings. Saugardas’s dated calendar use does not settle gard-/gerd- analysis. Ando/Anti retain the proposed Antonius alternatives; Andro remains unverified rather than borrowing Georgian/Croatian evidence.

[Woodrow](https://www.behindthename.com/name/woodrow) gives a row of houses by a wood; the Latvian catalogue retains forest-settlement/clearing alternatives, so Vudro’s full literal interpretation remains unverified. [Sabrina](https://www.behindthename.com/name/sabrina) supports the Severn/Habren family but leaves the river’s further meaning unknown; no princess legend is presented as fact. **EE-EKI** [lein](https://sonaveeb.ee/search/lite/est/lein/1/est) corroborates the common-word mourning gloss, not the personal-name derivation on its own.

No specific supported lexical proposal was found for **Sniga** or **Zanga**. Their next steps remain in the backlog. Exact-form queries with no matches are access/search outcomes, not proof that a name does not exist. The next fresh date pass is **6 December**.

[Huguette → Igeta](https://www.personvarduatveide.lv/words/40930?locale=lv), 1963 p. 77, adds a route alongside the catalogue’s Igita/Iveta proposals. [Honey → Hanija](https://www.personvarduatveide.lv/words/28463?locale=lv), Ahero 2006 p. 104, is a separate route from the proposed Hanna connection. Both names remain unverified. [Lucián → Luciāns](https://www.personvarduatveide.lv/words/17207?locale=lv), Sakse 1998 p. 55; [Lucian → Lucians](https://www.personvarduatveide.lv/words/29663?locale=lv), Ahero 2006 p. 77; [Lucy → Lūsija](https://www.personvarduatveide.lv/words/28648?locale=lv), Ahero 2006 p. 110. These are given-name rows. Luciāna’s female 1937 calendar record is explicitly not asserted as a masculine Luciāns date. [Ioana → Joana](https://www.personvarduatveide.lv/words/74123?locale=lv), Romanian recommendations 2025 p. 221; [Joanna → Joanna](https://www.personvarduatveide.lv/words/1150?locale=lv), Polish manual 1998 p. 55. Do not interchange Johanna’s calendar 1901 with Joanna’s 1767, or turn shared Jana/Jāna and Gaismona/Gaismone dates into separate first-birth claims.

**Broader family checks.** INT-SNL, Gulbrand Alhaug’s signed [Valdemar](https://snl.no/Valdemar_-_mannsnamn), describes Danish adaptation of Vladimir and calls a further German Waldo-mar connection possible. Siliņš’s German waltan/māri explanation does not settle one ultimate route for every related Latvian spelling: those profiles remain open. INT-BTN [Odilia](https://www.behindthename.com/name/odilia) gives uodil/heritage versus ot/wealth alternatives; Otīlija, Otilija and Odilija are not assigned a uniquely verified root. [Eleanor](https://www.behindthename.com/name/eleanor) leaves the further origin unresolved; Hannelora’s documented Johanna + Eleonora composition is retained without the old unproved “God is my light” gloss. [Lucianus](https://www.behindthename.com/name/lucianus) derives from Lucius, not from a feminine local attestation. [Loviise](https://www.behindthename.com/name/loviise), Louise and Ludwig establish the full hlud/hlut + wig family; the popular column’s bare fame gloss is incomplete. INT-DMNES [Joan](https://dmnes.org/name/Joan), England Latin Johanna 1246, PSS-II p. 6, is explicitly a related foreign episode for the LT feminine forms. [Daniel](https://dmnes.org/name/Daniel) supplies the full Hebrew “God is my judge”, rather than just “judge”. LT-VLE [Jonas Aistis](https://www.vle.lt/straipsnis/jonas-aistis/) documents the chosen literary name and *Be tėvynės brangios* (1942); its surname/literary use is not mistaken for a given-name birth record.

**New discovery route and access limits.** EE-EKI’s [personal-name index](https://arhiiv.eki.ee/nimeselts/bib/boisn.htm) and [given-name bibliography](https://arhiiv.eki.ee/nimeselts/bib/botm06.htm) locate **Annika Hussar, “Edvard ja Kelli”, Pere ja Kodu 2005, no. 6, p. 46**. The article itself has not been read, so its contents are not evidence yet. Kelli remains open between Kalli, Kerli/Gertrud and English Kelly proposals. DIGAR lists Edgar Rajandi’s actual book **Raamat nimedest**, Eesti Raamat, 1966 ([catalogue](https://www.digar.ee/arhiiv/en/books/236882)); public-network access is restricted. It is a library-access lead, not a consulted dictionary or a freely downloaded source. The Kaišiadorys library’s Aistis bibliography timed out; no unread book-title detail was accepted from it. EKI lite searches for eha, kild and ere returned no simple definition; only the opened [kuld](https://sonaveeb.ee/search/lite/est/kuld/1/est) page was used here as independent common-word corroboration, not personal-name etymology.

Reviewed **12 November 2026**. The most productive new resource is **EE-RAJANDI66**, Edgar Rajandi, *Raamat nimedest* (Tallinn, 1966), a full-text PDF in the University of Tartu DSpace repository: inspect page images, because its OCR layer misreads letters. The fetch tool now supports the documented promotion workflow: reusing a cached URL with a new --id creates an alias manifest for the **same content object**, without a network request. Reusing an existing ID for a different URL is rejected before fetching or overwriting anything. Regression checks cover both cases. Exact-spelling cache IDs in this work use a URL hash suffix to avoid collapsing Dāvids, Davids and Dāvīds; original bytes remain stored once by hash. The public source index lists documented directory/round IDs and counts only actual PDFs as cached PDFs; the private catalogue includes all HTML pages and aliases too.

### Checked negative leads and next inspections

- **LT-SALYS83 PDF 233 / printed 218**, visually inspected: exact Gùstis is short for Augustas or Augustinas. It is not Gustas, whose list also includes Gustavas. This resolves a missed text-layer lead but does not yet supply a separate dated episode. Gustis stays unverified as a full history.
- The [25 February 2024 Lrytas name article](https://www.lrytas.lt/gyvenimo-budas/psichologija/2024/02/25/news/vardu-reiksmes-vasario-26-kovo-3-d-varduvininkai-29271588) returned **HTTP 403** through the cache fetcher. Its search snippets for Gustis/Tolvaldas were not accepted. Reuse this failed result rather than repeating the fetch. A Salys Tol- search lead labels a related Tolvaldas as Latvian; it is not silently converted to Lithuanian evidence.
- Une hits were common-word or Norwegian-rendering contexts; Ulmi’s Rajandi index points to **EK 1937:128**, which remains an original to inspect. No dream/sleep etymology is inferred.
- Līva’s prose withholds a separate date despite the page header’s 1461; Endijs’s prose attributes 1973/1975 registrations to Endija. Neither header is promoted to an exact-form record. Marts/Mārts retain shared-entry and possible-1519 scope; Vents/Ventis retain shared 1942/1908 scope.
- Elvīna does not establish Elvina/Elvīne; Eveline does not establish Evelīne; Justins does not establish Justīns; Andriana/Andrianna does not establish Andriāna or Andrijana. Similarity and related-name fields alone were not accepted as formation evidence.
- Albo’s Finnish-source mark, Virma’s Lithuanian-calendar hit and the Latvian Austra/Aurora dates retain their actual country scope. They do not establish new histories for a different country.
- Every open form has an individual outcome and concrete next step in [round 97 notes](research/namedays/round97-notes.json). Exact-search absence is not evidence of historical non-use.

Sixteen profiles carried inherited reviewed-source provenance without a reviewed narrative. All were examined individually. Tālis’s prose refers to Tālivalds, not the related field’s Tālivaldis. The dawn-deity assertion for Aušra was not adopted.

## 7–21 March: round 98

Calendar-order pass for all LV/LT/EE records on 7–21 March (15 dates). Accounts for 380 calendar-profile records: 44 existing reviewed records preserved and 336 unfinished records examined (335 distinct unfinished profiles). Adds 94 histories in five languages; 241 distinct profiles remain unverified. A completed pass is not verified-complete. No new hypothesis is displayed. Next fresh date: 22 March. New histories: LV 50, LT 30, EE 14; two paragraphs in every supported language. Existing family narratives count as ready; inherited reviewed-source provenance alone does not. The 241 distinct open profiles occupy 242 calendar records (Laima occurs twice). Individual outcomes and next inspections are in [round 98 notes](research/namedays/round98-notes.json). Raw originals and page images remain private.

### Reused originals and claim limits

- **LT-SALYS83**: visually inspected PDF304/printed289 for March, including Vilė on 14 March; PDF303/288 for Vilys on 23 February; PDF306/291 for Anzelmas on 21 April; PDF316/301 for Silvija on 3 November; PDF317/302 for Filomenas on 22 November and Lukrecija on 23 November; PDF318/303 month heading and PDF319/304 for Gediminas (Gedas), 19 December. These are 1964 calendar recommendations, reprinted in 1983, not coining or first-bearer dates. Supplied calendar dates are preserved. PDF27/printed12 supports Tautas’s short-from-compound class. PDF148/133 and149/134 distinguish the later literary form Liutauras from chronicle spellings, including Hartknoch’s 1679 Lutuwerus; this is not proof of that modern spelling in a medieval original.
- **LT-PAKERYS11 PDF1/printed90**: exact Tautginė belongs to the reported **1934** Didysis calendar, not the 1927 list on the same page. Tautgintė is a separate form.
- **EE-RAJANDI66**: PDF148/printed150 Rudolf/Ruudi/Rolf;17/19 Ainar;66/68 and67/69 Rego;56/58 Ernst;125/127 Mat(h)ilde and Tilde;127/129 Meta/Meeta;173/175 and220/222 Valvo;64/66 Gerda;95/97 and205/207 Kertu;45/47 Eedi/Eedo;87/89 and88/90 Joosep. Historical samples retain their exact group and period. Ernst is an original name in a 1935–1940 name-change sample, not a birth count of its replacements. The Eedi/Eedo figure of 85 concerns original Eduard bearers collectively, not each replacement spelling. Meta’s dated literary episode concerns related Meeta. Kertu is not Kerttu. Rajandi’s printed Joosep literary title is not silently corrected into an exact-title quotation in the widget.
- **LV-ALL93 PDF5,7,8 / printed5,7,8**: Amalda and Imalda are genuine historical names despite gaps in the old dictionary. This does not by itself resolve their lexical origins. The separate 2009 Imalda family account retains its individual scope.

### Rejected or incomplete leads

- Erasts has prose about Erasta; Ulriks has prose about Ulrika at Aizpute in 1843; Jozefs has prose about Jozefa at Vecpiebalga in 1638. Žozefs’s Jāzepa reference needs grammatical/original-entry inspection. A page heading does not assign those dates to another form. Ēvalds, Ferdinands, Una and Ūnika have insufficient formation prose.
- Adelfina does not establish Adelfīna; Jēzups does not inherit Jezups; Guntārs does not inherit Guntars; Fabiāns/Fabijans/Fabijāns do not inherit Fabians. The original chronicle spelling behind Fabians’s 1227 catalogue date remains uninspected and is explicitly qualified. The catalogue’s city-of-Fabia gloss was not adopted.
- Imula hits concern a river; Raigardas is a place-name context; Kärdi is a place list; Türk’s 1834 Küllo Otza Jaan is a byname/place context. These do not establish personal-name etymologies. Milda/Milde’s historical group does not provide separate per-form totals. Malvi as a Mathilde replacement is not proof of lexical derivation.
- Salys prints Varuna, not Varūna. Tautginė and Tautgintė, Gaudvilė and Gaydvilė, and Galmantė and Galmė are kept distinct. Accent-insensitive discovery recovered additional Salys/Pakerys leads for Laima, Vydminas, Virmantas, Lionginas, Vita, Vytė, Josvydas, Tautvilė, Reda, Butgailė, Naubartas, Darmantė and Darmantas; exact original scope and remaining verification steps are recorded per name. No absence claim is made from an unsuccessful exact query.
- Unresolved hypotheses remain open. No new hypothesis is displayed, no spelling similarity is promoted to fact, and no historical population sample is presented as a current count.

### Checked negative leads

- Eiženija’s heading conflicts with Eižēnija in prose. Vidaga’s prose concerns Vīdaga. These dates/explanations are not assigned across the mismatch. Ģiedra, Izidors, Geralds and Sidors lack sufficient exact origin prose in their own entries; a related-name field alone was not accepted.
- Gēda’s actual2012-era corpus use is separate from the article’s qualified derivation proposal. Ģēda is a different initial. Grācija is not Gracija; the article prints Glīta, not Glita; Mārīte does not establish Marite. Žana in the article is an inflected Jean/Žans reference, not feminine nominative evidence. Dženifera accompanies another component’s analysis and does not gain a root from that context.
- Agija/Agijs, Ginta, Igunda, Ilgmārs, Gvido and Arp retain competing or questioned explanations. No such lead is silently promoted. Mere gender, spelling or common-word similarity does not supply a missing formation or historical episode.
- The primary2013 corpus does not resolve Daiva’s Latvian/Lithuanian alternatives. Ordinary vide, environment, and geographic/surname contexts are rejected as personal-name evidence. Kimmo in the Kimmu comparison and Marjo in a Finnish comparison do not supply separate Estonian dated bearers.
- Every open profile retains status needs_more and verification_status unverified, with its exact cache/original locators and next step. No new hypothesis is displayed, and none of these completed passes is declared verified-complete.

## 6–20 April: round 100

Calendar-order pass for all LV/LT/EE records on 6–20 April (15 dates). Accounts for 375 calendar-profile records: 52 existing reviewed records preserved and 323 unfinished records examined (322 distinct unfinished profiles). Adds 111 histories in five languages; 211 distinct profiles remain unverified. A completed pass is not verified-complete. No new hypothesis is displayed. Next fresh date: 21 April. Additions: LV 64, LT 29, EE 18; 555 translations and 1110 paragraphs. Readiness is the actual rendered narrative, including family narratives, rather than inherited provenance type. See [round 100 notes](research/namedays/round100-notes.json) for every examined profile, outcome and next step. A completed pass is not verified-complete. Raw originals, extracted text and page images remain private.

Reused primary evidence and limits:

- **LT-SALYS83**: original calendar PDF300/printed285 (1964 context), 301/286, 302/287, 304/289, 305/290, 306/291, 308/293, 309/294, 310/295, 311/296, 314/299, 316/301 and317/302. Exact individual pairs and source dates are in the notes. PDF284/printed269 classifies Dalia among ordinary-word name formations; it does not by itself prove a goddess or flower gloss. PDF103/printed88 discusses Karijotas, kari-/jot- and the cited Kor’iata1350 record; the medieval original was not independently inspected. Source-calendar dates are historical evidence, never automatic changes to project membership.
- **EE-RAJANDI66**: original PDF21/printed23,80/82,88/90,89/91,90/92,102/104,103/105,167/169,169/171,171/173,177/179,178/180,180/182,207/209 and219/221. Separate Lehe1884, Lehte1901 and Lehti1914; exact Udo/Uudo Tartu1930–1942 samples are distinct. Local index records are not nationwide first attestations. Other text-only hits remain discovery leads as individually recorded.
- **EE-MAGISTE29-AES**: original PDF28/printed22,56/50 and58/52. A1929 proposal is not a first bearer or coining date. Finnish Villo and Livonian Valdeko comparisons do not establish dated Estonian use.
- **LV-LVA-NORDIC03**: original PDF111/printed215, personal-name row Egil → Egils. This establishes normative rendering, without choosing a remote ancient root.
- **LV-PLESUMA-BALODE13**: original PDF62–63/printed60–61 establishes the study method and1 January2012 cutoff; PDF64–65/printed62–63 explicitly derives Orhideja from the plant word, and PDF73/printed71 analyses Floransa<Florentine and the full-name component Floriāns in Floriāns Ainārs<Floriānis. These are accepted scoped formations, not present-day counts or first uses. Other hits remain discovery leads.
- **LT-PAKERYS10**, **LT-PAKERYS11**, **LT-MACIEJAUSKIENE04**, **LV-ALL93** and **LV-LILE24**: cache discovery matches are retained with exact page locators in the open records. ## 26 May–4 June: round 105

Calendar-order pass for all LV/LT/EE records on 26 May–4 June (10 dates). Accounts for 307 calendar-profile records: 43 existing reviewed records preserved and 264 unfinished records examined (263 distinct unfinished profiles). Adds 76 histories in five languages; 187 distinct profiles remain unverified. A completed pass is not verified-complete. No new hypothesis is displayed. Next fresh date: 5 June. Additions: LV 37, LT 16, EE 23; 380 translations and 760 paragraphs. See [round 105 notes](research/namedays/round105-notes.json). Productive this round: LV-SILINS90 (printed pp. 84, 89, 103, 107, 116, 144, 180, 187, 207–208, 213, 217–219, 225–226, 249, 261, 267, 291, 304, 318, 326–327, 331), LT-SALYS83 (PDF308/printed293, page image transcribed: 21 May–8 June; corrects OCR Ronaldas → Konaldas, Aliejus → Alfėjus, Žiną → Žina), EE-RAJANDI66 (PDF27, 62, 74, 112, 130, 154, 164), EE-MAGISTE29-AES (PDF26, 55) and EE-MAGISTE36 (PDF35, 43). Note for Estonian sources: Rajandi’s and Mägiste’s “Kalda” is the genitive of Kallas (Oskar Kallas).
